about: Stable IDs of the checklist actions of this language. build.py matches every "- [ ] ..." item of a chapter checklist to the entry of the same chapter whose normalised text is equal (links, case, spacing, quotes and the effort tag in parentheses are ignored). The ID is the key under which a reader's tick is saved in the browser, so never rename or reuse one. Reworded an action? Update its "text" here to keep the ID. New or removed action? Run: python3 build.py --update-actions

actions.text: Install a private messenger, lock it with a PIN, hide your number and set disappearing messages
Move your 5 closest contacts and your family group
Verify the safety number of your 3 most important contacts
Install a second messenger that needs no phone number
Turn on encrypted backups in the apps you keep
Check your email address on Have I Been Pwned
Install a password manager and create a passphrase of 6 random words
Give your email a new unique password and turn on 2FA with an authenticator app, plus your 2 hardware keys if you bought them
Move your 4 next most important accounts and remove SMS codes where possible
Put your passphrase on paper in one safe place and your recovery codes in another, and tell 1 trusted person where
Change the default search engine on your computer and your phone
Install a browser that blocks tracking and make it your default
Add uBlock Origin where supported, or use your browser's blocker, and remove unused extensions
previous_texts: Add uBlock Origin, and remove the extensions you do not really use

actions.text: Move your Google and Facebook sessions to a second browser
Test your browser on coveryourtracks.eff.org
Open a mailbox at a provider funded by its users
Set up an alias service and its browser extension
Create your first alias and use it for your next signup
Move your 5 most important accounts to the new address
Forward the old mailbox and move the remaining accounts
Turn on encrypted DNS on your phone and in your browser
Choose and install a VPN from a trustworthy operator
Turn on the kill switch and auto-connect, then check for leaks
Install Tor Browser and try it once
Remove VPN apps whose operator or privacy practices you cannot trust
previous_texts: Remove any "free VPN" app from your devices

actions.text: List every key and recovery code you already have
Write the missing backups by hand and store them in 2 places
Test a recovery with a real recovery code
Tell a trusted person where your backups are
Buy 2 security keys and add them to your main accounts
Install a client and create your keys
Back up your nsec on paper or in your password manager
Fill your profile and follow a few people you already know
Install a signer and log in to a second client through it
Add a Lightning address to your profile and send your first zap
Request your data export from Google, Apple or Meta
Replace 1 easy service: search, maps or notes
Choose your first important service and run it in parallel for 2 weeks
Move the data and change defaults; delete the old cloud copy only after verifying an independent backup and disabling sync on devices you want to keep
previous_texts: Move the data, change the default on every device, delete the old copy

Uninstall the apps you no longer use
Review location, microphone, camera and contacts permissions
Delete the advertising ID or turn off tracking
Set a PIN of 6 digits or more, and a SIM PIN
On iPhone, turn on Advanced Data Protection. On Android, install F-Droid and try 1 app
Find a computer that can stay on, such as an old laptop, a mini PC or a Raspberry Pi
Install a platform and a first app
Set up automatic backups on a second disk, plus a copy off-site
Restore a file from the backup to check that it works
Choose a safe way to reach it from outside, and change every default password
Install 1 local AI app and download a small model
Turn off the network and check that the model still answers
Try it on a document you would never upload
Turn off training and chat history in the online assistants you keep
Write down what stays local, what may go online, and what no AI ever sees
Draw the map of where your savings are and who holds each part
Answer the 5 questions for your main account and your main investment
Check that no single bank or broker holds everything you own
Set aside a small cash reserve at home
Decide which self-held asset you want to learn first, and with what small amount
Install a self-custodial wallet from its official source, after checking the developer name and its page on walletscrutiny.com
Write the recovery words on paper before receiving anything
Receive a first payment larger than the setup fee and send some back
Install a second wallet from another team and compare
Move anything you left on an exchange to a wallet you control
Write your words by hand and check them twice
Remove digital seed copies; if exposure is possible, move funds safely to a fresh wallet, since deletion does not undo a leak
previous_texts: Delete any photo, note or file that contains them

actions.text: Make a second copy and store it in a second place
Test a tiny software wallet on a second device without deleting the original; check hardware backups only with the maker's hardware procedure
previous_texts: Test the recovery on a second device, without deleting the original app

actions.text: Write the sealed letter for your family and make a steel copy
Pay a Lightning invoice, at a merchant or a meetup
Get a Lightning address and test it from a second wallet
Find 3 places near you on btcmap.org
Withdraw any balance from a broker or exchange to your own wallet
Read how a peer-to-peer exchange works, before you need it
Check that your wallet shows a fresh address for every payment
Find any address or balance you have posted publicly, and stop receiving on those addresses
Create separate wallets for savings, spending and exchange withdrawals
Label every coin you own with its origin
Connect your wallet to your own node, after chapter 18
Decide what amount is "savings" for you and no longer belongs on a phone
Choose a device from the table and order it from the maker, to a pickup point
Check the device and its firmware the way the maker describes, create a new seed and a backup, then send a test amount
With only a tiny test balance, follow the maker's hardware backup-check or restore procedure before adding savings
previous_texts: Wipe the device and restore it from the backup

actions.text: Verify the address on the device screen at every receive
Look in your wallet's network settings and see which server it uses today
Verify the Bitcoin Core download, install it in pruned mode so it does not fill your disk, and watch it synchronise
Choose a platform and the hardware for a dedicated node, with a 2 TB SSD
Build the node, start the synchronisation (a few days, unattended) and add an Electrum server
Point your wallet to your own node and remove the public server
